source_name: Prva banka Crne Gore — Karijera
why_relevant: Domestic-owned bank; vacancy texts observed include international payment service head and payment-transaction operational roles, which map directly to payments capability build-out.

source_name: Hipotekarna banka — LinkedIn company page
why_relevant: Second-largest ME bank by assets; LinkedIn carries both job postings and employee-authored posts about new platforms, go-lives and vendor partnerships that never appear in formal disclosure.

source_name: INFINTECH — regional banking/fintech conference, Porto Montenegro
why_relevant: The single most concentrated ME weak-signal venue: agenda tracks (open banking, payments, data & AI, embedded finance), speaker list and — critically — the sponsor/partner roster identify which vendors are actively selling into Montenegrin banks and which bank executives own which programmes.

source_name: INFINTECH LinkedIn showcase page
why_relevant: Publishes sponsor and speaker announcements ahead of the website update; comments and reposts reveal which vendor teams are attending.

source_name: MFM Conference (Montenegro Finance & Markets), Hilton Podgorica
why_relevant: Senior-level ME finance conference; agenda covered payments-landscape evolution and AI in commerce, with the Minister of Finance, the CBCG Governor and the Capital Market Authority president as speakers. Speaker/panel composition reveals policy direction and which institutions are aligning on payments modernisation.

source_name: CBCG FinTech Hub / FinTech Hackathon
why_relevant: The Central Bank's own innovation channel. Hackathon themes (digital banking and payment services; KYC; open banking) are an explicit, dated statement of regulator priorities, and prize sponsorship (e.g. Mastercard alongside CBCG) exposes scheme-level relationships. Co-organised with ICT Cortex and the Association of Banks, which maps the domestic supplier network.

source_name: ICT Cortex — Montenegrin ICT cluster (members, internships, open positions)
why_relevant: Cluster of ~40 ME IT firms including Logate, which builds and maintains software systems for Montenegrin banks. Cluster member lists, aggregated open-position posts and its annual analysis of the top 30 ME IT companies map the domestic vendor bench that banks buy from, and hiring at those vendors is an even earlier signal than hiring at the banks.

source_name: IT SPOT — Montenegro's technology summit (ICT Cortex)
why_relevant: National tech summit (4th edition, Podgorica, 15-16 Oct 2026) with a published sponsor and strategic-partner roster including the Chamber of Economy. Bank and fintech participation, plus which vendors buy general sponsorship, is a direct read on where technology money is moving in ME.

source_name: TECHNOBANK — regional banking technologies conference & exhibition, Belgrade
why_relevant: The largest regional banking-technology conference (25th edition, ~500 financial-sector delegates, ~40 exhibitors; Payten as general sponsor). Montenegrin banks and their vendors attend; the exhibitor and sponsor roster is the clearest available map of who is selling what into the Western Balkans payments stack, and the Match & Meet programme lists bilateral vendor-bank meetings.

source_name: Balkan Payment Forum (ProMoney Events)
why_relevant: Regional payments forum gathering Western Balkan banks, regulators, fintechs and investors; speaker affiliations and sponsor list surface ME institutions' payment priorities and vendor courtship at a regional level.

source_name: Payten (Asseco SEE) — news & events
why_relevant: Dominant regional payments vendor. Its own event/news feed announces conference sponsorships, acquisitions (e.g. Necomplus) and client wins — a vendor-side mirror of bank technology decisions, often earlier and more explicit than the bank's own communication.

source_name: Zaposli.ME — IT job listings (Montenegro)
why_relevant: Described as the most-visited ME employment site; its IT category captures bank and bank-vendor engineering vacancies naming concrete platforms and stacks that never appear in official filings.

source_name: Posao Crna Gora (posao.crna.gora.me) — national business/jobs platform
why_relevant: Aggregated ME vacancy platform with company directory attached; useful for cross-checking bank vacancies and for resolving employer entities (adresar preduzeća) discovered elsewhere.

source_name: Prekoveze.me — employer job-ad pages (e.g. Crnogorska komercijalna banka)
why_relevant: Employer-scoped ME job aggregator that keeps a per-bank page with dated vacancies, giving an easy longitudinal hiring series per institution.

source_name: Careerjet Montenegro — 'posao banka' aggregated feed
why_relevant: Meta-aggregator that crawls many ME boards; a cheap safety net catching bank/payment vacancies posted on boards not individually tracked.

source_name: Digitalizuj.Me — ME digital/tech portal, 'takmičenje' tag
why_relevant: Covers ME hackathons, competitions, startup and ICT-cluster news; a low-cost pointer feed for discovering new fintech competitions and awards before they appear in mainstream banking media.

source_name: Privredna komora Crne Gore — Association of banking, other financial organisations and insurance
why_relevant: Chamber of Economy body that convenes sector events and is a named strategic partner of ME tech conferences; its event calendar and board composition point to which banks and vendors are organising sector gatherings.

source_name: AZZK — Agencija za zaštitu konkurencije Crne Gore (Agency for Protection of Competition), concentration decisions (Rješenja — koncentracije)
why_relevant: Merger clearance decisions are published as full-text PDFs and routinely quantify the Montenegrin banking/payments market: relevant market definition, participant market shares, turnover, rationale. Bank and payment-institution deals (e.g. NLB/Addiko, Alta Pay Group/Addiko filings referenced in 2024 case lists) pass through here, giving adversarial detail that banks do not disclose themselves.

source_name: AZZK — Restrictive agreements decisions (Restriktivni sporazumi)
why_relevant: Cartel/restrictive-agreement decisions would capture any coordinated fee-setting, interchange or bank-association arrangements; even negative outcomes reveal what was investigated in banking/cards.

source_name: AZZK — Abuse of dominant position decisions (Zloupotreba dominantnog položaja)
why_relevant: Abuse cases against banks, card schemes or payment processors would expose pricing, access and exclusivity practices, and typically contain market-share and dominance analysis for payments.

source_name: AZZK — Sectoral analyses (Sektorske analize)
why_relevant: Sector inquiries are the single richest quantified public description of a national market when they cover banking/payments — concentration ratios, fee comparisons, entry barriers.

source_name: AZZK — Annual reports and reports section (Izvještaji o radu)
why_relevant: Annual activity reports summarise all cases opened/closed by sector, giving a fast index of which banking/payment matters existed in a year, including cases whose decisions are not separately posted.

source_name: AZZK — State aid registry portal (Registri državne pomoći)
why_relevant: State aid records capture guarantee schemes, subsidised credit lines and bank-channelled support programmes — an indirect but quantified view of public money flowing through the banking sector.

source_name: CBCG — Zaštita prava klijenata kreditnih institucija i korisnika finansijskih usluga (Central Bank consumer-protection function)
why_relevant: The Central Bank's dedicated consumer-protection unit publishes statistics on controls performed, complaints considered, their merit, and measures imposed on credit institutions and payment service providers — the core complaint-channel dataset for this cell.

source_name: CBCG — Pravo na prigovor (right of complaint procedure page)
why_relevant: Defines the escalation path (bank internal complaint body -> CBCG) and deadlines; needed to interpret complaint volumes and to identify which institutions are named. Available in Montenegrin (/me/) and English (/e/).

source_name: CBCG — Naknade za usluge povezane sa računom za plaćanje potrošača (payment-account fee comparability disclosures)
why_relevant: Mandated fee-comparability publication under the Montenegrin transposition of EU Directive 2014/92/EU: standardised, cross-bank fee data for consumer payment accounts — the quantitative backbone for any pricing/consumer-detriment analysis, and the trigger for many complaints.

source_name: CBCG — Regulativa: podzakonski akti, zaštita korisnika potrošačkih kredita
why_relevant: Secondary legislation governing consumer-credit protection and the Decision on the manner and deadlines for reporting client complaints — defines exactly what complaint data banks must report to CBCG, hence what can be requested or expected to be published.

source_name: CBCG — Godišnji izvještaj o radu (Central Bank annual activity report)
why_relevant: Contains an annual chapter on consumer/user protection with complaint counts, supervisory measures and sanctions against banks, plus payments-infrastructure milestones (e.g. SEPA accession). Stable, machine-readable PDF series.
